This iconic dish is celebrated for its harmonious blend of mild spices, buttery indulgence, and a hint of sweetness, making it a comforting and flavorful meal. instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with yogurt, 1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste, lemon juice, turmeric powder, red chili powder, garam masala, and 1/2 teaspoon salt. Mix well to ensure all chicken pieces are coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or preferably 2-4 hours for best flavor.

instructions.title: Cook the Chicken
instructions.text: Heat 1 tablespoon of butter in a large pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken in batches, ensuring not to overcrowd the pan. Cook until browned on all sides and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes per batch. Remove cooked chicken and set aside.

instructions.title: Prepare the Sauce Base
instructions.text: In the same pan, melt the remaining 3 tablespoons of butter over medium heat. Add the finely chopped onion and cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the remaining 1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste and green chilies (if using), and cook for another 2 minutes until fragrant.

instructions.title: Simmer the Tomato Mixture
instructions.text: Drain the soaked cashews and add them to the pan along with the crushed tomatoes. Stir well. Bring the mixture to a simmer, then reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 10-15 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the tomatoes to soften.

instructions.title: Blend the Sauce
instructions.text: Carefully transfer the tomato and cashew mixture to a blender. Blend until completely smooth and creamy. For an extra silky sauce, you can pass it through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pan. This step ensures no cashew bits or onion chunks remain.

instructions.title: Combine Chicken and Sauce
instructions.text: Return the smooth sauce to the pan over medium-low heat. Add the cooked chicken pieces and 1/2 cup of water. Stir gently to combine. Simmer for another 5-7 minutes, allowing the chicken to absorb the rich flavors of the sauce.

instructions.title: Finish and Serve
instructions.text: Stir in the sugar, crushed kasoori methi, and heavy cream. Mix well and heat through for 1-2 minutes, but do not boil after adding the cream. Taste and adjust salt and sugar if needed. Garnish generously with fresh chopped cilantro and serve hot with naan bread, roti, or basmati rice.

tips: For an even richer flavor, char the marinated chicken slightly in a tandoor or under a broiler before adding to the sauce. This adds a smoky depth.
Adjust the level of spice by varying the amount of red chili powder and green chilies. For a milder dish, omit the green chilies entirely.
Kasoori Methi (dried fenugreek leaves) is crucial for authentic flavor; crush it between your palms just before adding to the sauce to release its aromatic oils.
article:
Butter Chicken, known authentically as Murgh Makhani, is more than just a dish; it's a global culinary icon. Its irresistible creamy, rich, and mildly spiced tomato gravy enveloping succulent pieces of chicken has captivated taste buds worldwide. Originating from the bustling streets of Delhi, this Indian chicken recipe has transcended borders, becoming a staple in Indian restaurants and a beloved comfort food for many. If you've been searching for the ultimate Butter Chicken Recipe, look no further. This article will guide you through the journey of creating this classic, offering insights into its history, authentic ingredients, step-by-step preparation, and expert tips to ensure your homemade version is nothing short of spectacular.

## What is Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani)?

Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani (meaning "butter chicken" in Hindi), is a quintessential Indian curry that originated in the Moti Mahal restaurant in Delhi in the 1950s. It was reportedly created by Kundan Lal Gujral, who experimented with leftover tandoori chicken by simmering it in a rich tomato-based gravy made with butter, cream, and a blend of spices. The result was a revelation: tender chicken bathed in a velvety, slightly sweet, and tangy sauce with a subtle smokiness. Its distinct flavor profile comes from a harmonious blend of tomatoes, ginger, garlic, green chilies, and aromatic spices like garam masala and fenugreek leaves (kasoori methi), all mellowed by a generous amount of butter and cream. Murgh Makhani is celebrated for its luxurious texture and balanced flavors, making it one of the most popular Indian chicken recipes globally.

## Ingredients for Authentic Butter Chicken

Crafting an authentic Butter Chicken Recipe requires attention to quality ingredients. Here's what you'll need:

For the Chicken Marinade:
*   500g boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breast, cut into 1-inch pieces
*   1/2 cup plain full-fat yogurt
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder (Kashmiri chili powder for color, or regular for heat)
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1 teaspoon garam masala
*   Juice of 1/2 lemon
*   Salt to taste

For the Rich Gravy:
*   2 tablespoons unsalted butter, plus extra for finishing
*   1 tablespoon cooking oil
*   1 large onion, finely chopped
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1 green chili, slit (optional, for mild heat)
*   800g canned crushed tomatoes or 6-7 large ripe tomatoes, pureed
*   1/2 cup cashews (soaked in warm water for 15-20 minutes, then blended into a paste)
*   1/2 cup heavy cream, plus extra for garnish
*   1 tablespoon kasoori methi (dried fenugreek leaves), lightly toasted and crushed
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1 teaspoon garam masala
*   1-2 teaspoons sugar (adjust to balance tanginess)
*   Salt to taste
*   Fresh coriander, chopped, for garnish

## Step-by-Step Instructions to Make Butter Chicken

Creating this beloved Indian chicken recipe at home is a rewarding experience. Follow these steps for a perfect Butter Chicken Recipe:

1.  **Marinate the Chicken:** In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with all marinade ingredients. Mix well, ensuring each piece is coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or preferably 2-4 hours for maximum flavor and tenderness.
2.  **Cook the Chicken:** Heat a tablespoon of oil in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer, without overcrowding the pan. Cook until lightly browned and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes per side. Set aside. You can also grill or bake the chicken for a more authentic tandoori flavor.
3.  **Prepare the Gravy Base:** In the same pan, melt 2 tablespoons of butter with 1 tablespoon of oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onions and sauté until translucent and soft, about 5-7 minutes. Stir in the ginger-garlic paste and green chili (if using), cooking for another minute until fragrant.
4.  **Add Tomatoes and Cashews:** Pour in the crushed or pureed tomatoes. Add the soaked cashew paste, red chili powder, turmeric powder, and garam masala. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 10-15 minutes, allowing the mixture to simmer and thicken, and the oil to separate from the sides.
5.  **Blend the Gravy:** Remove the pan from heat and let the mixture cool slightly. Carefully transfer the gravy base to a blender and blend until completely smooth. For an extra velvety texture, pass the blended gravy through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pan.
6.  **Finish the Gravy:** Return the pan with the strained gravy to medium-low heat. Stir in the sugar and salt to taste. Add the cooked chicken pieces. Pour in the heavy cream and the crushed kasoori methi. Simmer gently for another 5-10 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the chicken to absorb the rich gravy. Stir in an extra knob of butter just before serving for that signature 'butter' richness.
7.  **Garnish and Serve:** Garnish with fresh chopped coriander and a drizzle of extra cream.

## Pro Tips for the Best Butter Chicken Results

To elevate your homemade Butter Chicken Recipe from good to unforgettable, consider these expert tips:

*   **Marination is Key:** The longer you marinate the chicken, the more tender and flavorful it will be. Overnight marination is ideal.
*   **Don't Overcook the Chicken:** Cook the chicken just enough to brown it and cook it through. It will finish cooking in the gravy, preventing it from becoming dry.
*   **Smooth Gravy:** Blending the gravy base thoroughly and then straining it through a sieve ensures an incredibly smooth and luxurious texture, free of any onion or tomato bits.
*   **Kasoori Methi:** Lightly toast the kasoori methi in a dry pan for a minute before crushing it between your palms. This enhances its aromatic flavor significantly.
*   **Balance of Flavors:** Butter Chicken is all about balance. Taste and adjust the sugar (for sweetness and to cut the tang of tomatoes) and salt as needed. A squeeze of lemon juice at the end can brighten the flavors.
*   **Use Quality Ingredients:** Fresh, ripe tomatoes (or good quality canned tomatoes) and full-fat dairy products make a noticeable difference in the final taste and texture.
*   **The Butter Finish:** Don't skip adding extra butter at the very end. It contributes to the authentic richness and gloss of the dish.

## Serving Suggestions for Murgh Makhani

This classic Butter Chicken Recipe pairs wonderfully with a variety of Indian breads and rice dishes, making it a complete and satisfying meal.

*   **Naan Bread:** Soft, fluffy naan bread (plain, garlic, or butter naan) is perfect for scooping up every last bit of that luscious gravy.
*   **Basmati Rice:** Steamed basmati rice or fragrant jeera rice (cumin rice) provides a lovely contrast to the richness of the curry.
*   **Roti or Paratha:** Whole wheat flatbreads like roti or flaky paratha also make excellent accompaniments.
*   **Accompaniments:** A simple side salad of sliced red onions, a wedge of lemon, and a dollop of cooling raita (yogurt with cucumber and spices) can complement the richness and add a refreshing element to your meal.
*   **Garnish:** Always garnish with fresh coriander leaves and a swirl of heavy cream for presentation and an extra touch of freshness.

## Variations and Substitutions for Butter Chicken

While the classic Butter Chicken Recipe is divine, don't hesitate to experiment with variations and substitutions to suit dietary needs or personal preferences.

*   **Vegetarian/Vegan Options:** For a vegetarian version, substitute chicken with paneer (Indian cottage cheese), tofu, or mixed vegetables (like cauliflower, peas, and potatoes). For a vegan Butter Chicken, use plant-based butter, coconut cream instead of dairy cream, and substitute chicken with tofu or chickpeas.
*   **Healthier Twist:** Reduce the amount of butter and cream, or opt for low-fat cream. You can also increase the vegetable content by blending roasted bell peppers into the gravy for added nutrients and color without compromising flavor too much.
*   **Spice Level:** Adjust the amount of red chili powder and green chilies to your liking. For a milder curry, omit the green chili and use less red chili powder. For more heat, add an extra chili or a pinch of cayenne pepper.
*   **Smoky Flavor (Dhungaar):** For an authentic smoky flavor reminiscent of tandoor-cooked chicken, use the "Dhungaar" method. Heat a small piece of charcoal until red hot, place it in a small steel bowl in the center of your curry, drizzle a teaspoon of ghee or oil over it, and quickly cover the pot for a few minutes to infuse the smoke.

Mastering this Butter Chicken Recipe is a culinary achievement that brings the heart of Indian cuisine into your home. With its vibrant flavors and comforting texture, Murgh Makhani is a dish that promises to impress and satisfy every time. So gather your ingredients, follow these steps, and prepare to indulge in one of the world's most cherished Indian chicken recipes. Enjoy the journey of creating this classic, and savor every bite of your homemade Butter Chicken!
